question: Which of the following was the famous ruler of the Satavahana dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gautamiputra Satakarni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gautamiputra Satakarni** is considered the greatest ruler of the Satavahana dynasty and ruled during the 1st–2nd centuries CE.
 
• He revived the power of the Satavahanas by defeating the Shakas (Western Kshatrapas) and re-establishing control over the Deccan region.
 
• His reign is well-documented in the **Nashik Prashasti (inscription)**, composed by his mother Gautami Balashri, which highlights his military conquests and administrative achievements.
 
• He was known as a defender of Brahmanism and patronized Vedic rituals like the **Rajasuya and Ashvamedha**, emphasizing his role as a Dharmic ruler.
 
• Under his rule, the Satavahana kingdom extended over a vast area, including parts of modern-day Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Karnataka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satavahana Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Satavahanas were one of the earliest Indian dynasties to issue coins with inscriptions, reflecting their administrative and economic sophistication.
 
• They are credited with promoting trade and commerce, especially through the port of Sopara, connecting India with the Roman Empire.
 
• The Satavahanas were known for their contributions to **art and architecture**, including the development of Buddhist stupas such as the Amaravati and Sanchi stupas.
 
 
 
• **Nashik Inscription:**
 
 
• Also known as the Nashik Prashasti, it was inscribed by Gautamiputra Satakarni’s mother, Gautami Balashri, and is a crucial source of information about his reign.
 
• The inscription highlights his victories against the Shakas, Pahlavas, and Yavanas, establishing him as a powerful ruler in the Deccan region.
 
 
 
• **Western Kshatrapas:**
 
 
• The Western Kshatrapas were the primary rivals of the Satavahanas during Gautamiputra Satakarni’s reign.
 
• They ruled parts of modern-day Gujarat and Maharashtra and were eventually subdued by the Satavahanas under Gautamiputra’s leadership.
 
 
 
• **Vedic Rituals:**
 
 
• Gautamiputra Satakarni's performance of Rajasuya and Ashvamedha reflected his authority as a sovereign ruler.
 
• These rituals were significant in ancient Indian political culture, symbolizing the ruler’s legitimacy and dominance.
